changes.before: Return a note label that falls back only when its optional detail is missing.
changes.after: Use backup text only when an optional detail is missing.

before: An optional property may be absent from an object. Write ? after its name in the type.
With strict null checking, an optional string property is read as string | undefined. Check for absence before calling a string method on it.
The ?? operator uses its fallback for null or undefined. Unlike ||, it preserves an empty string.
A readonly property cannot be reassigned through that typed reference. This is a compiler restriction, not a runtime freeze.
For the exercise, label({title: "Read"}) returns "Read: No detail". A present detail is kept exactly, including an empty string. Return a label without changing the note.
after: An optional property does not have to be present on an object. Write a question mark after its name in the type.
In `note?: string`, the question mark makes note optional. If the object has no note, reading that property gives `undefined`, meaning no value is there.
With strict checking, an optional text property may be string or undefined. Check that it exists before using a text method on it.
An empty string is still a present text value. This function keeps it empty. The `||` operator would replace empty text with the backup, which is different.
A readonly property cannot be reassigned through that typed reference. For example, `readonly title: string` lets you read the title but prevents assigning a new title through that type.
Readonly is a TypeScript checking rule. It does not freeze the object while JavaScript runs.
Make label return the note's title, a colon and space, then its detail. Use No detail only when the detail is missing. Keep a present empty string and leave the object unchanged.

before.question: label uses note.detail ?? "No detail". Someone replaces ?? with ||. What changes for {title:"Draw", detail:""}?
choices: Nothing; both operators only replace undefined
before.explanation: An empty string is falsy, so || chooses the fallback. ?? preserves it because it is neither null nor undefined.

after.question: If ?? is replaced by ||, what happens to a detail that is an empty string?
choices: It becomes the backup text No detail
after.explanation: The || operator replaces empty text. The ?? operator keeps it because empty text is neither null nor undefined.

changes.before: Prerequisites: typescript-01 and JavaScript object/string access. Verify with strict TypeScript checking as well as runtime cases. A readonly annotation does not freeze the object at runtime. Compile-negative examples: assigning note.title, passing detail: 5, or calling an optional detail method without narrowing must be rejected. No external-data validation is implied.
changes.after: The checks cover missing detail, empty detail, wrong value types, and readonly title. Readonly helps the checker; it does not freeze outside data.

project.title: Handle a missing detail
project.task: Return a note label with No detail only when the detail is missing.
project.done_when: Missing detail gets the backup, empty text stays empty, the note stays unchanged, and the checks pass.
